description:
Goal: Return canonical bottom from nominal struct construction when its final required field map contains canonical bottom, sharing the proven plain-map field-building rule without a second traversal or changed duplicate-key semantics.

Signal: `Types::struct_map` still passes a pair iterator into `Descr::struct_map`, which builds a map descriptor and sends a known-impossible product to generic normalization. `MapSig` emptiness treats required fields of both plain and nominal map tags alike: a final bottom-valued field makes the product empty. The just-completed plain-map path established the correct complication: duplicate input keys are resolved last-write-wins.

Strategy: Extract the final-required-field builder from `Types::map`. It builds exactly one ordered `BTreeMap` and tracks a bottom-valued final field as insertions replace values. Apply it to `Types::struct_map`; let `Descr::struct_map` receive the owned final map directly. Do not add an extra scan, cache, hash, deep comparison, or broad record-normalization change.

TDD: Establish a red interior-bottom struct test with interning-work counts. Prove an earlier bottom overwritten by a later inhabited field remains an inhabited struct with that field type. Preserve the plain-map proof while centralizing the common builder.

Docs and acceptance: Extend the product-field documentation to include nominal structs. Run focused type tests and enum/f98 canaries, fmt, check, strict Clippy, full workspace tests, cold branch-base review, one commit, draft stacked PR, and close.
title: Return impossible structs before descriptor normalization
